The standing hypothesis at src/UiSpike.cpp:3479-3480 ("that band height scales 11 -> 22 / 33, both exact, but 11 -> 16.5 at 1.5x") names the wrong number. 11 is the DESTINATION window height (area 120,57,222,68), not a band.
findings.evidence: Decoded all 26 rows of the 102x26 1x PNG. Each row is a full centre-zero diverging ladder: 12 red cells left (x=0..46, 3px cell + 1px FF00FF key, pitch 4, starts 0,4,8..44), a (172,179,175) centre cell x=49..52, then 12 cells right (x=55..101, same 3/1 pitch). Row 0 = 12 red (36 red px, brightest FF0000 at x=0 grading to D50000 at x=44); row 1 = 11 red (33 px); ... row 11 = 1 red (3 px); rows 12 AND 13 = zero (0 red, 0 green, byte-identical, md5 dcfd3460); row 14 = 1 green (3 px) ... row 25 = 12 green (36 px, 00FE00/00FF00 at x=100,101). Red px per row descends exactly 36,33,30,27,24,21,18,15,12,9,6,3 and green ascends 3,6,...,36 — a 3-px-per-state staircase. 25 distinct row-frames at 1x. findings.claim: THE 1.5x-ONLY VERTICAL DEFECT: with band height 1, 1*1.5 = 1.5 is fractional, and nearest-neighbour makes the filmstrip RAGGED — 12 of the 24 states get 2 output rows and 12 get 1. At 2x and 3x every state is exactly 2 and exactly 3 rows, so state*factor is a provable no-op. There is NO integer band height at 1.5x.
findings.evidence: Frame-height histograms measured by grouping identical rows: 1x {1:24, 2:1}; 1.5x {1:12, 2:12, 3:1}; 2x {2:24, 4:1}; 3x {3:24, 6:1}. (The one outlier per tier is the zero state, which is 2 source rows by design: rows 12-13.) Exact 1.5x frame starts: 0,2,3,5,6,8,9,11,12,14,15,17,18,21,23,24,26,27,29,30,32,33,35,36,38 — i.e. ceil(state*1.5), which alternates +2,+1,+2,+1. At 2x starts are 0,2,4,...,50 (uniform +2); at 3x 0,3,6,...,75 (uniform +3). Consequence: any consumer computing srcY = state * bandHeight with an integer bandHeight lands on the WRONG frame at 1.5x for every state where ceil(s*1.5) != s*round(1.5) — floor(s*1.5) is wrong for all 12 odd states, and bandHeight=1 addresses only frames 0..16 of 25 (top 2/3 of the range, the bar never reaching full). Only floor(s*1.5+0.5) (law 89) lands correctly on all 25.
findings.tierSignature: 1x uniform 1 / 1.5x RAGGED 2,1,2,1... / 2x uniform 2 / 3x uniform 3

findings.claim: A SECOND, FULLY INDEPENDENT 1.5x-ONLY DEFECT, PURELY HORIZONTAL: the LEFT (red) half and the RIGHT (green) half of every row have DIFFERENT tick geometry at 1.5x. Red ticks are 5px with 1px gaps; green ticks are 4px with 2px gaps. At 1x/2x/3x the two halves are identical. This needs no assumption about the Y axis at all and is directly "look at their formatting".

THE CAUSE OF THE HORIZONTAL ASYMMETRY IS A HALF-PIXEL SOURCE-ORIGIN PHASE that exists only at 1.5x. The red block's origin is x=0 (phase 0 at every factor), but the centre cell starts at x=49 and the green block at x=55 — both ODD, so at 1.5x they land on .5 and shift the nearest-neighbour sampling phase of every right-hand cell. At 2x and 3x all three origins stay integers.
findings.evidence: 1x block origins measured: red x=0, centre cell x=49, green x=55. Scaled: 0*1.5=0.0 (frac .0), 49*1.5=73.5 (frac .5), 55*1.5=82.5 (frac .5). At 2x: 0.0 / 98.0 / 110.0 — all frac .0. At 3x: 0.0 / 147.0 / 165.0 — all frac .0. Measured spans confirm the half-pixel is real and conserved: red block span 47 (1x) -> 71 (1.5x, ideal 70.5, GAINS 0.5) -> 94 (2x) -> 141 (3x); green block span 47 -> 70 (1.5x, ideal 70.5, LOSES 0.5) -> 94 -> 141. Centre-of-mass of the centre cell: 1x 50.5 of 102 (dead centre 50.5, exact); 1.5x 76.5 of 153 (dead centre 76.0 — 0.5px RIGHT of centre); 2x 101.5 of 204 (exact); 3x 152.5 of 306 (exact). The pitch itself is fine at every tier (red cell starts 0,6,12..66 at 1.5x — uniform 6 = 4*1.5); it is only the cell:gap SPLIT that goes wrong, and only on the odd-origin side.
